message.content:
**Quick note:**  
`docker start <container>` starts a *running* container, **not** the Docker Engine itself.  
If you’re looking to bring up the Docker service (so you can then run `docker ps`, `docker run`, etc.), you’ll need to start the Docker Desktop app or the underlying Windows service that runs the Docker Engine.

---

### 1️⃣ Start Docker Desktop (GUI)

The simplest way:

1. Click the **Docker Desktop** icon from your Start menu or taskbar.  
2. Wait until the whale icon turns blue – that means the engine is ready.

> ⚠️ If you don’t see the icon, install Docker Desktop first: https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop

---

### 2️⃣ Start the Docker Engine Service (CLI)

If you prefer the command line (or need to script it), you can start the Windows service that powers Docker Desktop:

| Shell | Command |
|-------|---------|
| **PowerShell** | `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` |
| **Command Prompt** | `sc start com.docker.service` |
| **PowerShell (as admin)** | `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service -Verbose` |

> 🔧 Make sure you run the shell as Administrator; otherwise you’ll get “Access denied”.

After running one of those commands, wait a few seconds for the service to initialize. You can verify it’s running with:

```powershell
Get-Service -Name com.docker.service
```

or

```cmd
sc query com.docker.service
```

When the status shows `RUNNING`, the Docker Engine is up and you can now issue normal Docker CLI commands (`docker ps`, `docker run`, etc.).

---

### 3️⃣ Verify Docker is Ready

Once the service is running, check connectivity:

```bash
docker version
docker info
```

Both should return without errors. If you still see “Cannot connect to the Docker daemon”, double‑check that the service status is `RUNNING` and that you’re using the correct context (`docker context ls`).

---

#### TL;DR

- **To start Docker Desktop (the GUI):** Launch the app from the Start menu.  
- **To start the Docker Engine via CLI:** Run `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` (PowerShell) or `sc start com.docker.service` (CMD).  

After that, you can use `docker start <container>` to bring up individual containers.
